candidates.title: Embodied carbon as a mandatory project 'gate', not a report
candidates.shift: A conceptual framework proposes embedding embodied-carbon accounting directly into construction project governance as a decision gate, not a voluntary disclosure appended after design.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: if adopted, developers/retailers would need carbon budgets approved before permitting proceeds, reshaping site selection and materials sourcing timelines — still conceptual, worth watching.
candidates.evidence: Conceptual framework paper proposing embodied-carbon lifecycle governance gates for new built assets.
candidates.source: Research Journal of Pure Science and Technology
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from carbon accounting as after-the-fact reporting to a mandatory pre-construction governance checkpoint; driven by rising embodied-carbon share of building emissions. If widespread, store construction/renovation would require carbon sign-off before groundbreaking.
candidates.author: Bahaaaldeen M. Abdulhadi

candidates.title: Drones enter the delivery scheduling stack, not just the pilot program
candidates.shift: Researchers model centralized scheduling that treats riders and delivery drones as one interchangeable fleet for urban instant delivery under a 'low-altitude economy' framing.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: directly touches the open 'delivery format?' hunt zone — implies stores/DCs may need drone launch/landing infrastructure and reworked curb-parking allocation, not just app-side routing.
candidates.evidence: Scientific Reports study on centralized rider-drone collaborative scheduling for urban instant delivery.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from purely ground-based last-mile logistics to hybrid ground-air fleets modeled as one scheduling problem; if operationalized, retail sites need drone docking zones and revised airspace-adjacent parking design.
candidates.author: Shuai Huang, Tianyu Fu, Bo Zhang

candidates.title: Accessibility gets measured as a network, not a doorway
candidates.shift: A new model optimizes barrier-free walking routes across whole communities (using points-of-interest and space-syntax data) rather than assessing accessibility building-by-building.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: as populations age, retail site accessibility scoring could shift from ADA-style entrance compliance to network-level 'last block' connectivity metrics.
candidates.evidence: Study proposing community-level barrier-free route optimization integrating POI and space-syntax data for age-friendly design.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from building-level accessibility compliance to network-level accessible-route scoring for aging communities; could reshape how retailers evaluate site accessibility beyond parking and entrance design.
candidates.author: Jing Zhang

candidates.title: A framework to judge dead retail/office by its neighborhood, not just its shell
candidates.shift: A new evaluation framework (PARS) argues that residential adaptive-reuse decisions should weigh surrounding urban context, not just building-level characteristics, amid housing shortages.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: an absence being filled — current dead-mall/office-to-housing conversion tools ignore infrastructure capacity; this could formalize criteria that accelerate or block store-to-housing conversions.
candidates.evidence: Computational Urban Science paper proposing an urban-context framework (PARS) for residential adaptive reuse of non-residential buildings.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from building-only adaptive-reuse assessment to context-aware frameworks weighing surrounding infrastructure; if adopted by planners, could accelerate dead retail/office-to-housing conversion and reshape asset valuation.
candidates.author: Esma Selen Aksoy, Birgül Çolakoğlu

candidates.title: Heat-risk maps may be quietly wrong where data is thin
candidates.shift: A study finds that small temperature-interpolation errors in data-sparse regions substantially distort heat-wave detection.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: implies climate-risk models used to insure or site stores in under-monitored geographies (much of the Global South) may be systematically miscalibrated — an absence in current risk pricing.
candidates.evidence: Research Square preprint showing spatial interpolation errors alter heat-wave detection despite small raw temperature errors in data-sparse regions.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from assumed uniform reliability of climate data to recognition that heat-risk detection is unreliable in data-sparse regions; implies insurers and real-estate investors are underpricing heat exposure for assets in peripheral geographies.
candidates.author: Fabiano Fernandes Bargos, Maurí­cio Lamano Ferreira, Danúbia Caporusso Bargos

candidates.title: Digital Product Passports: consumers will pay for labels but won't read them
candidates.shift: A behavioral experiment finds a gap between willingness-to-pay for green attributes and willingness-to-engage with detailed Digital Product Passport (DPP) information under the EU's circular economy plan.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative absence: retailers lack in-store UX/checkout tech to surface DPP data meaningfully — the passport exists on paper before the interface does.
candidates.evidence: Environmental and Resource Economics behavioral experiment on consumer engagement with Digital Product Passport information.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from static sustainability labels to mandated interactive per-product data passports; if consumer engagement lags, retailers may need in-store kiosks or staff training to bridge the gap, changing checkout and merchandising design.
candidates.author: Zack Dorner, Steven Tucker, Abraham Zhang et al.

candidates.title: A carve-out hides where affordable-housing money actually goes
candidates.shift: Oregon spends record amounts on low-income housing while a public-records law carve-out shields the spending details from disclosure.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: as affordable-housing capital flows grow nationally, this could become a template — or cautionary case — for how public real-estate finance builds in opacity by design.
candidates.evidence: Reporting on Oregon's public-records law carve-out shielding low-income housing spending details despite record state spending.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from assumed transparency in public capital deployment to legally sanctioned opacity in affordable-housing finance; could normalize reduced accountability in public-private real estate financing structures elsewhere.

candidates.title: AI reaches the dumpling shop before the department store
candidates.shift: A small independent Chinese food retailer adopts AI tools for daily operations, framed nationally as a productivity-force narrative.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative, peripheral-geography signal: AI diffusing into micro/independent retail labor and task decomposition ahead of, or parallel to, enterprise chain rollout in the West.
candidates.evidence: Rest of World profile of a Chinese dumpling shop owner adopting AI, framed via 'science and technology as productive force' rhetoric.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from AI adoption as an enterprise-scale story to AI reaching micro/independent retail operators from the bottom up; if the pattern spreads, small-format store labor and task decomposition could change before top-down chain rollout does.
candidates.author: Viola Zhou

candidates.title: Public plaza furniture that also does the stormwater engineer's job
candidates.shift: A modular urban-furniture prototype in Quito manages rainwater and biodiversity while doubling as public seating/park infrastructure, installable on any surface.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative, peripheral-geography (Ecuador, Kichwa-named) design could set a transferable retrofit standard for hard-surface parking lots and plazas at retail sites globally.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily coverage of the Yaku modular stormwater/biodiversity furniture prototype installed in Quito's Isla Tortuga Park.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from fixed, engineered stormwater infrastructure to modular, retrofittable urban furniture managing runoff anywhere; retail sites with hard-surface parking could adopt similar modules to meet climate-resilience codes.
candidates.author: Valentina Díaz
